result.summary: Track the memory footprint of transactions retained solely by active block templates after removal from the mempool. Add reference-counting bookkeeping to BlockTemplateManager and expose a getMemoryLoad() IPC query so external clients can monitor template memory consumption.
result.problem: When external IPC mining clients hold references to block templates, transactions evicted or replaced in the mempool remain pinned in memory. Node operators and IPC clients have no visibility into how much memory stale or held templates are consuming.
evidence: Discussion and issue #33899: "Block template memory management (for IPC clients)"
Demonstrated client-side integration in Stratum v2 template provider (stratum-mining/sv2-tp#63)
result.scope_notes: Moves CTransactionRefComp and helper hasher logic to util/hasher.h for reuse in BlockTemplateManager. Adds a dedicated fuzz target for BlockTemplateManager.
result.changed_since_previous: The prerequisite PR 35675 introducing BlockTemplateManager has merged; this PR no longer has pending base dependencies.
result.card: Tracks memory usage of transactions pinned exclusively by open block templates after their removal from the mempool. Adds reference counting to BlockTemplateManager and exposes a getMemoryLoad() method over the IPC mining interface so external clients like Stratum v2 template providers can detect and release memory pressure. The change provides observability for process-separated mining setups without altering block construction or consensus behavior.

risk.why: A flaw in reference counting or memory calculation could lead to inaccurate metrics or an assertion failure during template destruction, but does not affect consensus or block generation.
